record: AISEF V2 — CYCLE-2 OWNER DECISIONS (DECISION-1..6), as issued
authority: owner decision 'AISEF V2 — CYCLE-2 OWNER DECISIONS / WP-2.0.1 AUTHORIZATION' (2026-09-28)
study_accepted: The Cycle-2 architecture study is ACCEPTED for implementation planning. Commit 35f0d0d is accepted as harness hygiene only. Cycle-1 semantic baseline remains immutable.
authorized: WP-2.0.1 ONLY. Do NOT start downstream Cycle-2 packages yet. Do NOT start the first production probe implementation until owner acceptance.

decisions.subject: universal criteria witness sets
decisions.owner_text: Finite witness sets are a measurement strategy only. They MUST NOT silently convert a universal requirement into a sampled requirement. For every affected criterion record the quantifier semantics explicitly: exhaustive over a finite declared domain; bounded witness measurement; or unsupported for FULL enforcement. If FULL universal enforcement cannot be provided, the probe must declare the appropriate weaker enforcement or refuse admission. No "N examples passed => universal property proven".
mechanical_consequences: every contract derived from a universally quantified criterion carries a declared quantifier_semantics of exactly one of: exhaustive_finite_domain, bounded_witness_measurement, unsupported_for_full_enforcement
a probe answering a bounded witness measurement declares an enforcement level below FULL for that class, or the spec is refused at admission (UNSUPPORTED -> INVALID_SPEC)
no verdict derived from witnesses is recorded as a proof of the universal property; the ProbeResult detail names the witness set
applies_to: WP-2.2.2, WP-2.3.1 (class tables and enforcement declarations)

decisions.subject: controlled process-effect fault step
decisions.owner_text: It MUST be: harness-owned; a closed typed vocabulary; content-addressed; part of probe/capability identity; deterministic; bounded by StoryScope/ProcessRange authority. Forbidden: arbitrary callback; arbitrary shell; developer-authored executable fault step; subject output expanding destructive authority.
mechanical_consequences: the fault step is a member of the closed scenario step vocabulary (an Enum; Q0 CLOSED_DISPATCH_IN_SCENARIO_PROBES); its parameters are a fixed typed shape, never a callable, a shell string or a developer file
the fault vocabulary is part of the process_effect probe's source and therefore of its digest and capability identity
the step runs inside the harness's own process range under the StoryScope; nothing the subject prints or returns can select, widen or trigger a fault or any disposal (INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY)

decisions.subject: six test-named LedgerLock criteria
decisions.owner_text: Draft PLAN-V2.2 mappings from test-named criteria to actual product subjects/observables. Do NOT approve the contracts automatically. Do NOT run LedgerLock with PLAN-V2.2. Return the six exact before/after mappings for owner review.
mechanical_consequences: WP-2.5.1 produces LEDGERLOCK-PLAN-V2.2-PROPOSAL with six before/after mappings; the contracts carry no approval record
no LedgerLock run under PLAN-V2.2 until the owner approves the mappings; QP-2.9 runs only an approved plan
the P10 record (PLAN-V2.1, NOT_REACHED) is never retuned or re-interpreted

decisions.subject: two-invocation equality
decisions.owner_text: Implement as two independent observations under one harness-owned probe contract. Bind: both stimuli; revision; probe identity; normalization policy; equality comparator. Equality MUST NOT depend on wall-clock timing, shared mutable cache, checkout metadata, or previous invocation residue.
mechanical_consequences: an equality observable names both stimuli, the normalization policy and the comparator inside the ProductProofSpec, so all of them enter semantic_hash together with revision and probe identity
the two observations run in two fresh evaluation directories of the same revision under the same probe; the comparator reads the two normalized results only
Q0 NO_CLOCK_IN_PROBE_FACTS and the hidden-authority matrix rows (bytecode cache, cwd, residue) apply to both observations

decisions.subject: LedgerLock PlanQualityPolicy
decisions.owner_text: DO NOT preregister plan-quality thresholds for the Cycle-2 LedgerLock regression. LedgerLock remains DEVELOPMENT_REGRESSION. For its Cycle-2 rerun: plan_quality_verdict = NOT_CLAIMED. Raw plan-quality metrics are still recorded. Thresholds belong to future preregistered sealed workloads only.
mechanical_consequences: no PLAN-QUALITY-POLICY.json is written for LedgerLock; validation/qualification/p10.py's plan_quality_verdict_of yields NOT_CLAIMED
raw plan-quality metrics are recorded descriptively, as in Cycle 1
the Workload state machine keeps LedgerLock at DEVELOPMENT; SEALED/HOLDOUT/EVALUATING refused mechanically

decisions.subject: python_callable extensions
decisions.owner_text: KEEP the Cycle-1 python_callable implementation and digest unchanged: 1961e84d... New observation classes MUST ship under a SECOND probe identity. Do not mutate the Cycle-1 probe implementation merely to add: returns_bytes; constant equality; workspace stimulus; richer raises attributes. Existing Cycle-1 ProductProofSpec / semantic_hash evidence remains tied to the original probe. The new probe must have independent: probe_id; probe_digest; capability calibration; falsifiability evidence; mutation evidence; Q1/Q2/Q3 coverage.
mechanical_consequences: aisef2/probe/protocol.py and aisef2/probe/python_callable.py stay byte-identical to the parent's blobs (cycle2_baseline R2); the live digest is checked against the frozen 1961e84d… on every run

the second identity is a new module with its own PROBE_ID, DIGEST, METADATA, CLASSES, calibration fixture root, mutation targets and Q1/Q2/Q3 coverage; it supersedes the Cycle-1 entry as the one active probe for subject kind python_callable (F4 binds one probe per kind at compile time) while the Cycle-1 entry stays registered so its evidence keeps its observation class (aisef2/probe/catalog.py)
no Cycle-1 ProductProofSpec is recompiled; new specs compile against the second identity only

f5_hard_guard: During WP-2.0.1 and every later probe package: if any proposed probe kind requires changing the Probe protocol shape, the ProbeResult shape, the observation-harness / subject split, enforcement semantics, execution-status semantics, owner routing, the ProductProofSpec compiler contract or frozen F1–F11 semantics: STOP, produce an ARCHITECTURE_EXCEPTION proposal, do not implement around it.
